claims.claim: Theodore of Heraclea was a bishop of Heraclea in Thrace (also called Perinthus) who held office sometime between AD 328 and 355.
He was a leading member of the Eusebian party that supported the Arian‑leaning bishops of Nicomedia and opposed Athanasius of Alexandria.

The fragments are valuable because they show how a mid‑fourth‑century Antiochene‑style exegete employed terms like πρόσωπον and ὑπόστασις to argue against Monarchianism and illustrate the theological disputes of the Eusebian alliance.
The work also demonstrates the transmission of early patristic commentary through the catena tradition, informing modern studies of the development of biblical exegesis.
